verses.original: Ἦσαν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ēsan de autō engizontes pantes hoi telōnai kai hoi hamartōloi akouein autou
verses.literal: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus
verses.literalPt: E CHEGAVAM-SE a ele todos os publicanos e pecadores para o ouvir.

verses.original: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: kai diegongyzon hoi te Pharisaioi kai hoi grammateis legontes hoti Houtos hamartōlous prosdechetai kai synesthiei autois
verses.literal: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble - This man welcomes sinners and eats with them
verses.literalPt: E os fariseus e os escribas murmuravam, dizendo: Este recebe pecadores, e come com eles.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων
verses.transliteration: Eipen de pros autous tēn parabolēn tautēn legōn
verses.literal: Then Jesus told . . . them this parable
verses.literalPt: E ele lhes propôs esta parábola, dizendo:

verses.original: Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ἀπολέσας ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό
verses.transliteration: Tis anthrōpos ex hymōn echōn hekaton probata kai apolesas ex autōn hen ou kataleipei ta enenēkonta ennea en tē erēmō kai poreuetai epi to apolōlos heōs heurē auto
verses.literal: What man among you if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them does not leave the ninety-nine . . . in the pasture and go after the one that is lost until he finds it
verses.literalPt: Que homem dentre vós, tendo cem ovelhas, e perdendo uma delas, não deixa no deserto as noventa e nove, e não vai após a perdida até que venha a achá-la?

verses.original: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους αὐτοῦ χαίρων
verses.transliteration: kai heurōn epitithēsin epi tous ōmous autou chairōn
verses.literal: And when he finds it he joyfully puts it . . . on his shoulders
verses.literalPt: E achando-a, a põe sobre os seus ombros, gostoso;

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συνκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας λέγων αὐτοῖς Συνχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός
verses.transliteration: kai elthōn eis ton oikon synkalei tous philous kai tous geitonas legōn autois Syncharēte moi hoti heuron to probaton mou to apolōlos
verses.literal: comes home and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them Rejoice with me for I have found my lost sheep
verses.literalPt: E, chegando a casa, convoca os amigos e vizinhos, dizendo-lhes: Alegrai-vos comigo, porque já achei a minha ovelha perdida.

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας
verses.transliteration: legō hymin hoti houtōs chara en tō ouranō estai epi heni hamartōlō metanoounti ē epi enenēkonta ennea dikaiois hoitines ou chreian echousin metanoias
verses.literal: I tell you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine . . . righteous ones who do not need to repent
verses.literalPt: Digo-vos que assim haverá alegria no céu por um pecador que se arrepende, mais do que por noventa e nove justos que não necessitam de arrependimento.

verses.original: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως οὗ εὕρῃ
verses.transliteration: Ē tis gynē drachmas echousa deka ean apolesē drachmēn mian ouchi haptei lychnon kai saroi tēn oikian kai zētei epimelōs heōs hou heurē
verses.literal: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp sweep her house and search carefully until she finds it
verses.literalPt: Ou qual a mulher que, tendo dez dracmas, se perder uma dracma, não acende a candeia, e varre a casa, e busca com diligência até a achar?

verses.original: καὶ εὑροῦσα συνκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα Συνχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα
verses.transliteration: kai heurousa synkalei tas philas kai geitonas legousa Syncharēte moi hoti heuron tēn drachmēn hēn apōlesa
verses.literal: And when she finds it she calls together her friends and neighbors to say Rejoice with me for I have found my lost coin
verses.literalPt: E achando-a, convoca as amigas e vizinhas, dizendo: Alegrai-vos comigo, porque já achei a dracma perdida.

verses.original: οὕτως λέγω ὑμῖν γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι
verses.transliteration: houtōs legō hymin ginetai chara enōpion tōn angelōn tou Theou epi heni hamartōlō metanoounti
verses.literal: In the same way I tell you there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents
verses.literalPt: Assim vos digo que há alegria diante dos anjos de Deus por um pecador que se arrepende.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δέ Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν δύο υἱούς
verses.transliteration: Eipen de Anthrōpos tis eichen dyo huious
verses.literal: Then Jesus said There was a man who had two sons
verses.literalPt: E disse: Um certo homem tinha dois filhos;

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ νεώτερος αὐτῶν τῷ πατρί Πάτερ δός μοι τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος τῆς οὐσίας ὁ δὲ διεῖλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν βίον
verses.transliteration: kai eipen ho neōteros autōn tō patri Pater dos moi to epiballon meros tēs ousias ho de dieilen autois ton bion
verses.literal: The younger son said to him Father give me my share of the estate So he divided his property between them
verses.literalPt: E o mais moço deles disse ao pai: Pai, dá-me a parte dos bens que me pertence. E ele repartiu por eles a fazenda.

verses.original: Καὶ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας συναγαγὼν πάντα ὁ νεώτερος υἱὸς ἀπεδήμησεν εἰς χώραν μακράν καὶ ἐκεῖ διεσκόρπισεν τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτοῦ ζῶν ἀσώτως
verses.transliteration: Kai met’ ou pollas hēmeras synagagōn panta ho neōteros huios apedēmēsen eis chōran makran kai ekei dieskorpisen tēn ousian autou zōn asōtōs
verses.literal: After a few days the younger son got everything together . . . and journeyed to a distant country where he squandered his wealth in wild living
verses.literalPt: E, poucos dias depois, o filho mais novo, ajuntando tudo, partiu para uma terra longínqua, e ali desperdiçou os seus bens, vivendo dissolutamente.

verses.original: Δαπανήσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἰσχυρὰ κατὰ τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ αὐτὸς ἤρξατο ὑστερεῖσθαι
verses.transliteration: Dapanēsantos de autou panta egeneto limos ischyra kata tēn chōran ekeinēn kai autos ērxato hystereisthai
verses.literal: After he had spent all he had a severe famine swept through that country and he began to be in need
verses.literalPt: E, havendo ele gastado tudo, houve naquela terra uma grande fome, e começou a padecer necessidades.

verses.original: καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐκολλήθη ἑνὶ τῶν πολιτῶν τῆς χώρας ἐκείνης καὶ ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν εἰς τοὺς ἀγροὺς αὐτοῦ βόσκειν χοίρους
verses.transliteration: kai poreutheis ekollēthē heni tōn politōn tēs chōras ekeinēs kai epempsen auton eis tous agrous autou boskein choirous
verses.literal: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs
verses.literalPt: E foi, e chegou-se a um dos cidadãos daquela terra, o qual o mandou para os seus campos, a apascentar porcos.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπεθύμει γεμίσαι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν κερατίων ὧν ἤσθιον οἱ χοῖροι καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδίδου αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: kai epethymei gemisai tēn koilian autou ek tōn keratiōn hōn ēsthion hoi choiroi kai oudeis edidou autō
verses.literal: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating but no one would give him a thing
verses.literalPt: E desejava encher o seu estômago com as bolotas que os porcos comiam, e ninguém lhe dava nada.

verses.original: Εἰς ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἐλθὼν ἔφη Πόσοι μίσθιοι τοῦ πατρός μου περισσεύονται ἄρτων ἐγὼ δὲ λιμῷ ὧδε ἀπόλλυμαι
verses.transliteration: Eis heauton de elthōn ephē Posoi misthioi tou patros mou perisseuontai artōn egō de limō hōde apollymai
verses.literal: Finally he came to his senses and said How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food but here I am starving to death
verses.literalPt: E, tornando em si, disse: Quantos jornaleiros de meu pai têm abundância de pão, e eu aqui pereço de fome!

verses.original: ἀναστὰς πορεύσομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτῷ Πάτερ ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου
verses.transliteration: anastas poreusomai pros ton patera mou kai erō autō Pater hēmarton eis ton ouranon kai enōpion sou
verses.literal: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him Father I have sinned against heaven and against you
verses.literalPt: Levantar-me-ei, e irei ter com meu pai, e dir-lhe-ei: Pai, pequei contra o céu e perante ti;

verses.original: οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου
verses.transliteration: ouketi eimi axios klēthēnai huios sou poiēson me hōs hena tōn misthiōn sou
verses.literal: I am no longer worthy to be called your son Make me like one of your hired servants
verses.literalPt: Já não sou digno de ser chamado teu filho; faze-me como um dos teus jornaleiros.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰς ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος εἶδεν αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη καὶ δραμὼν ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Kai anastas ēlthen pros ton patera heautou eti de autou makran apechontos eiden auton ho patēr autou kai esplanchnisthē kai dramōn epepesen epi ton trachēlon autou kai katephilēsen auton
verses.literal: So he got up and went to his father But while he was still in the distance his father saw him and was filled with compassion He ran to his son embraced him . . . . . . . . . . . . and kissed him
verses.literalPt: E, levantando-se, foi para seu pai; e, quando ainda estava longe, viu-o seu pai, e se moveu de íntima compaixão e, correndo, lançou-se-lhe ao pescoço e o beijou.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ Πάτερ ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου
verses.transliteration: Eipen de ho huios autō Pater hēmarton eis ton ouranon kai enōpion sou ouketi eimi axios klēthēnai huios sou
verses.literal: The son declared Father I have sinned against heaven and against you I am no longer worthy to be called your son
verses.literalPt: E o filho lhe disse: Pai, pequei contra o céu e perante ti, e já não sou digno de ser chamado teu filho.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ Ταχὺ ἐξενέγκατε στολὴν τὴν πρώτην καὶ ἐνδύσατε αὐτόν καὶ δότε δακτύλιον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ὑποδήματα εἰς τοὺς πόδας
verses.transliteration: Eipen de ho patēr pros tous doulous autou Tachy exenenkate stolēn tēn prōtēn kai endysate auton kai dote daktylion eis tēn cheira autou kai hypodēmata eis tous podas
verses.literal: But the father said to his servants Quick Bring the best robe and put it on him Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet
verses.literalPt: Mas o pai disse aos seus servos: Trazei depressa a melhor roupa; e vesti-lho, e ponde-lhe um anel na mão, e alparcas nos pés;

verses.original: καὶ φέρετε τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν θύσατε καὶ φαγόντες εὐφρανθῶμεν
verses.transliteration: kai pherete ton moschon ton siteuton thysate kai phagontes euphranthōmen
verses.literal: Bring the fattened calf and kill it Let us feast and celebrate
verses.literalPt: E trazei o bezerro cevado, e matai-o; e comamos, e alegremo-nos;

verses.original: ὅτι οὗτος ὁ υἱός μου νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἀνέζησεν ἦν ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη καὶ ἤρξαντο εὐφραίνεσθαι
verses.transliteration: hoti houtos ho huios mou nekros ēn kai anezēsen ēn apolōlōs kai heurethē kai ērxanto euphrainesthai
verses.literal: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again He was lost and is found So they began to celebrate
verses.literalPt: Porque este meu filho estava morto, e reviveu, tinha-se perdido, e foi achado. E começaram a alegrar-se.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐν ἀγρῷ καὶ ὡς ἐρχόμενος ἤγγισεν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἤκουσεν συμφωνίας καὶ χορῶν
verses.transliteration: Ēn de ho huios autou ho presbyteros en agrō kai hōs erchomenos ēngisen tē oikia ēkousen symphōnias kai chorōn
verses.literal: Meanwhile the older son was in the field and as he approached . . . the house he heard music and dancing
verses.literalPt: E o seu filho mais velho estava no campo; e quando veio, e chegou perto de casa, ouviu a música e as danças.

verses.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα τῶν παίδων ἐπυνθάνετο τί ἂν εἴη ταῦτα
verses.transliteration: kai proskalesamenos hena tōn paidōn epynthaneto ti an eiē tauta
verses.literal: So he called one of the servants and asked what . . . was going on . . .
verses.literalPt: E, chamando um dos servos, perguntou-lhe que era aquilo.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἥκει καὶ ἔθυσεν ὁ πατήρ σου τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν ὅτι ὑγιαίνοντα αὐτὸν ἀπέλαβεν
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen autō hoti Ho adelphos sou hēkei kai ethysen ho patēr sou ton moschon ton siteuton hoti hygiainonta auton apelaben
verses.literal: Your brother has returned - he said - and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has him back . . . safe and sound
verses.literalPt: E ele lhe disse: Veio teu irmão; e teu pai matou o bezerro cevado, porque o recebeu são e salvo.

verses.original: Ὠργίσθη δὲ καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν εἰσελθεῖν ὁ δὲ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐξελθὼν παρεκάλει αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Ōrgisthē de kai ouk ēthelen eiselthein ho de patēr autou exelthōn parekalei auton
verses.literal: The older son became angry and refused to go in So his father came out and pleaded with him
verses.literalPt: Mas ele se indignou, e não queria entrar.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰδοὺ τοσαῦτα ἔτη δουλεύω σοι καὶ οὐδέποτε ἐντολήν σου παρῆλθον καὶ ἐμοὶ οὐδέποτε ἔδωκας ἔριφον ἵνα μετὰ τῶν φίλων μου εὐφρανθῶ
verses.transliteration: Ho de apokritheis eipen tō patri autou Idou tosauta etē douleuō soi kai oudepote entolēn sou parēlthon kai emoi oudepote edōkas eriphon hina meta tōn philōn mou euphranthō
verses.literal: But he answered . . . . . . his father Look all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends
verses.literalPt: E saindo o pai, instava com ele. Mas, respondendo ele, disse ao pai: Eis que te sirvo há tantos anos, sem nunca transgredir o teu mandamento, e nunca me deste um cabrito para alegrar-me com os meus amigos;

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ὁ υἱός σου οὗτος ὁ καταφαγών σου τὸν βίον μετὰ πορνῶν ἦλθεν ἔθυσας αὐτῷ τὸν σιτευτὸν μόσχον
verses.transliteration: hote de ho huios sou houtos ho kataphagōn sou ton bion meta pornōn ēlthen ethysas autō ton siteuton moschon
verses.literal: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes you kill the fattened calf for him
verses.literalPt: Vindo, porém, este teu filho, que desperdiçou os teus bens com as meretrizes, mataste-lhe o bezerro cevado.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τέκνον σὺ πάντοτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἶ καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐμὰ σά ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen autō Teknon sy pantote met’ emou ei kai panta ta ema sa estin
verses.literal: Son you are always with me - the father said and all that is mine is yours
verses.literalPt: E ele lhe disse: Filho, tu sempre estás comigo, e todas as minhas coisas são tuas;

verses.original: εὐφρανθῆναι δὲ καὶ χαρῆναι ἔδει ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου οὗτος νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἔζησεν καὶ ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη
verses.transliteration: euphranthēnai de kai charēnai edei hoti ho adelphos sou houtos nekros ēn kai ezēsen kai apolōlōs kai heurethē
verses.literal: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again he was lost and is found
verses.literalPt: Mas era justo alegrarmo-nos e folgarmos, porque este teu irmão estava morto, e reviveu; e tinha-se perdido, e achou-se.
